connectHelp.trigger: How do I connect a device?
connectHelp.title: Enable debugging on your Android
connectHelp.description: Before connecting, you need to enable Developer Options and debugging on the phone.

steps: Go to Settings → About phone, and tap "Build number" 7 times until you see "You are now a developer!".
Go back to Settings → System → Developer options (on some manufacturers it's directly under Settings, not under System).
Connect the phone to your PC with a USB cable.
A "Allow USB debugging?" dialog appears on the phone — accept it (check "always allow from this computer" so it doesn't ask again).
Enable Developer options (see the USB tab) and turn on "Wireless debugging".
Tap "Wireless debugging" → "Pair device with pairing code".
The phone shows an IP address, a pairing port, and a 6-digit code.
In ADBScope, open "+ Connect" → WiFi tab → "Pair", and enter those three values.
Once paired, use the IP and port shown on the main "Wireless debugging" screen (different from the pairing port) to connect.
wifi.note: Pairing only happens once per network — after that, just connect using the IP and port shown on the phone.

connectDialog.title: Connect a device
connectDialog.description: USB devices are detected automatically. WiFi devices need to connect manually.
connectDialog.usbHint: Plug the device in and enable USB debugging. It'll show up in the device list automatically.
connectDialog.pairHint: Android 11+: Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. Use the IP/port from that screen (not the main one) — they're different.
connectDialog.connectHint: Already paired (or on older Android)? Connect using the IP/port from the main Wireless debugging screen.
